payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When setup runs an inline sh -c script, the output shall show the target and a short label for the step, not the script text.
- When the script prints a message, the output shall still show it.
- When a scripted step fails, the error shall still name the step.
payload.description:
When terminal-setup runs a step as sh -c with an inline script, I want to see a short label for the step instead of the whole script, so I can read the output without mistaking the script's own guard messages for warnings. On 2026-09-25 the user ran terminal-setup --only config from Windows and read 'Claude Code not detected ($HOME/.claude missing)' as a warning. It was only the text of the script being printed; the step then ran and wrote 26 skills in WSL.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Run uvx --from git+https://github.com/niksavis/terminal@v0.8.0 terminal-setup --only config on a machine with ~/.claude present.
- Read the lines for the status line, img-zoom skill and cli-tools skills steps: each prints the sh -c script, which contains a 'Claude Code not detected ... missing' echo.
payload.requirements: One change in the runner used by every sh -c call site, with a regression test; verified by a dry run of --only config.
payload.title: Setup output shows a label, not the shell script, for scripted steps

payload.name: close_reason
payload.value: Runner.run and Reporter.command take a label; the console prints the command up to -c or -Command followed by the label, never the script. Every sh -c, bash -c and PowerShell -Command step that echoes is labelled; _run_shell_command and _run_in_wsl_or_host require it, and an AST scan found no caller without one. Unlabelled commands still print in full. Script output and errors are unchanged. Tests: 270 pass, also with is_running_in_wsl forced False; new tests cover the label rendering, the -Command cut and the three Claude steps on Windows. Consumer check: --dry-run --only config from the working tree via uvx, inside WSL and under Windows uvx.exe; every run line is a label, and no 'not detected' text appears.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When a GitHub-release tool is missing, setup shall install the latest release binary into ~/.local/bin after checking it against the release asset's sha256 digest, and refuse it on a mismatch.
- When such a tool is installed at the latest version, setup shall skip it and say so; when it is older, setup shall skip it and name the --update flag; with --update it shall install the latest.
- When zsh, tree, podman, bubblewrap or socat are missing in WSL, setup shall ask once to run sudo apt update, apt upgrade and apt install for exactly the missing packages, and print that command when declined or not interactive.
- When no Docker CLI package is installed, the apt step shall include podman-docker; otherwise it shall leave it out.
- When setup runs on Windows, tool-tree shall not be written for a tree found under the Windows System32 directory.
payload.description: When terminal-setup runs against a fresh Ubuntu WSL distro, I want to get every tool and the system packages it needs in one run, so I can start agentic work without a second installation. Canonical's WSL image manifests (24.04.5 and 26.04.1, the default that wsl --install picks per Microsoft's DistributionInfo.json) hold no gcc or libc6-dev, no zsh, no tree, no podman and no socat; 24.04 also lacks bubblewrap. Setup builds nine tools with cargo, which needs cc, and skips zsh and tree with a warning. Every tool's latest GitHub release publishes a Linux binary with a sha256 digest in the release API. Claude Code's sandbox on WSL2 needs bubblewrap and socat (code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing). podman-docker conflicts with docker.io and docker-ce-cli, so it must not replace an installed Docker. Windows tree resolves to System32 tree.com, so tool-tree is written for the wrong program.
payload.requirements: No compiler and no rustup in the default path; one table of release tools; regression tests per rule; README and CHANGELOG updated; released as v0.9.0.
payload.title: Fresh WSL: install every tool without a compiler and offer one sudo apt step

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When curl resolves under the Windows system directory, setup shall write tool-curl.
- When tree resolves to the Windows system tree.com, setup shall not write tool-tree.
payload.description:
When setup runs from Windows, I want tool-curl written for the curl.exe Windows ships, so I can have Claude Code know curl there too. v0.9.0 ignored every command found under the Windows system directory to skip tree.com, which is not GNU tree; that also skipped <redacted:windows-drive-path>, which is real curl (curl 8.21.0 on 2026-09-25). Found by the post-release check on v0.9.2.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Run uvx --from git+https://github.com/niksavis/terminal@v0.9.2 terminal-setup on Windows with no other curl on PATH.
- List %USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills: tool-curl is missing while curl.exe is on PATH.
payload.requirements: One named list of Windows built-ins that are a different program, with a regression test; released as v0.9.3.
payload.title: Windows skill detection drops the real curl.exe under System32

payload.value: WINDOWS_BUILTIN_IMPOSTORS names the one mapped command whose Windows built-in is a different program (tree, tree.com); only those are ignored under the system directory, so the real System32 curl.exe (curl 8.21.0) keeps tool-curl. A scan of System32 for every mapped command name found only curl.exe and tree.com. The regression test covers both.
